what_this_is: The numbers the discovery map runs on, as data rather than as constants in the screen, so that a critic can perturb them and watch the map change (RI-MTH07 CONSUMPTION). Nothing here is a marker, a route or a destination. There is no field in this file, and no field in any file, by which a quest can name a place to reveal.

reveal.note: How much ground one stop reveals. NOT invented: it is the REGION'S OWN declared sightline (game/data/world/regions.json `sightline_m`), clamped. Blackwood declares 18 m under a 0.965 canopy and the Stone Wastes declare 1400 m of open pan, so a walk through the forest leaves a thread on the map and the same walk across the wastes leaves a swathe. The province decides what the map looks like, which is the point of drawing the map from the province.
reveal.source: regions.json[].sightline_m, sampled at the player's own position
reveal.min_m_why: You always reveal the ground under your feet and the cell around it. Below ~40 m the 25 m raster cannot represent the disc at all and the map becomes a dotted line of single cells, which reads as damage rather than as darkness.
reveal.max_m_why: Above ~450 m the map stops being a record of where you have been and becomes a record of which direction you once faced. Valus Ridge declares 2200 m; honouring it literally would reveal a fifth of the province from one hilltop.
reveal.occlusion: NOT modelled. A hill between you and the ground does not stop that ground being revealed. This is deliberate and is recorded rather than hidden: per-cell line-of-sight over the height raster is affordable but it would make the revealed shape depend on terrain the player cannot see on the map, and the result would read as a rendering fault. If this is ever wrong, it is wrong in the direction of revealing MORE than was strictly seen.
reveal.how_to_disagree: Set min_m and max_m equal to make the reveal uniform across the province, or set both to 0 to reveal only the cell the player stands in. tools/harness/map-probe.mjs C1 reads the revealed-cell count and the drawn terrain area at three settings and asserts they differ; a build in which changing these numbers changes nothing has a disconnected model and the probe says so.

places.note: When a place is DISCOVERED. S35: 'any square for a place the player has not personally stood in' is a hard fail, so the test is standing, not seeing, not being told, and not being sent. The radius is the site's OWN built pad from game/data/world/terrain.json `sites[].r_flat` — the flat ground the settlement or landmark is built on — so 'stood in Stormhold' means 'stood on Stormhold's ground' and no number here was chosen by this piece.
places.source: terrain.json sites[].r_flat, matched to pois.json by id
places.fallback_radius_why: The 8 waystations in pois.json have no entry in terrain.json `sites` — they are not built pads, they are a shelter and a well. 25 m is one terrain cell: you have to be at it, not near it.
places.interiors: Discovery is SUSPENDED while sim.env.interior is set. An interior is a separate space whose exterior coordinates are meaningless, and observing there would paint the raster at whatever the body's exterior position happens to be. You discover a settlement by standing in it, which you did on the way to the door.
places.how_to_disagree: Raise fallback_radius_m to 500 and the waystations discover themselves from the road. map-probe C4 walks to a place and asserts the square appears, and asserts it was absent one frame before arrival.

draw.note: Colour comes from the region raster and the region palette, so the map cannot drift from the province: recolour a region in regions.json and the map recolours. There is no authored map image anywhere in this build.
draw.shade_from: terrain.json channels.base_dm — the same height the collision surface uses
draw.undiscovered_why: S35: 'Undiscovered is not merely unlabelled, it is unrendered.' This colour is the screen's own ground, not a fogged or dimmed version of the terrain — there is nothing underneath it to dim. A build that draws the province at 15% opacity and calls it undiscovered has drawn the province.
draw.local_span_why: S35 permits 'a local view for the cell you are in'. 500 m across is the settlement and its approach — Stormhold's built pad is 135 m — at a scale where individual revealed cells are legible instead of being one pixel each.
forbidden_by_construction: roads: game/data/world/roads.json is NOT loaded by the map screen. S35 forbids 'a route, path, trail or line of any kind' and a drawn road is a line. Wayfinding is the signposts' job (world/signposts.json) and the spoken directions' (dialogue/road-directions.json), both of which work with the map closed.
no distances, no bearings, no coordinates, and no numerals of any kind are drawn on either view
no place can be selected to travel to; the map's only input is which discovered place is being named

provenance: reveal.source and places.source are read off the BUILT world at runtime, not transcribed. min_m, max_m, fallback_radius_m, shade_range and local_span_m are constructed by W1-MAP and each carries its reason above.
